App.description: Where the app is described: a compose file only, for now (Helm, Kustomize and manifests come later).

compose.description: The compose file's path in the repository, e.g. deploy/compose.yaml. Left out, compose.yaml (or compose.yml, docker-compose.yaml…) at the root.

Build.description: A service's image: built from the repository, or one built elsewhere.

context.description: Built from this directory in the repository, e.g. "." or services/api.

dockerfile.description: With context: the Dockerfile's path, from the context.

image.description: Pulled as it is, e.g. ghcr.io/acme/api:${STAGD_SHA}: pushed by CI.

target.description: With context: the Dockerfile's stage to build.

wait.description: With image: how long to keep trying to pull it, as CI may push it after the deploy starts; between 1m and 2h. Left out, a missing image fails the deploy at once.

handled.description: What happens to a /stagd comment once it's handled: delete (the default), collapse or keep.

Config.description:
Config is a repository's stagd.yaml, as Stagd reads it: the optional file at the repository's root that says where the app is described and what Stagd adds on top.

The messages have stagd.yaml's own shape: a message's JSON (protojson, with the proto field names) is the file in its plain form. A file may also use a few shorthands, which read as their plain form:

  previews: always           previews: { when: always }
  services: { mail: true }   services: { mail: {} }
  mail: false (or otel)      left out

A reader fills in the defaults, e.g. a Neon database's name, and gives durations as protojson's ("1200s" for 20m). Who may open previews is never set here: a pull request mustn't be able to loosen its own preview's access by editing a file. That's set in Stagd.

stagd/config/v1/testdata in the stagd repository holds files with how they read, or the problems they have: every reader runs them.

build.description: Where each service's image comes from, by the compose file's service name.

comment.description: Added to the pull request comment once the preview is live, e.g. how to sign in. Markdown.

compute.description: The compute connection previews run on, by its name on Settings → Compute, e.g. kind. Left out, the org's default.

env.description: Variables the compose file can use, like compose's .env file. Values may use Stagd's variables and secrets, ${STAGD_PR_NUMBER} or ${SESSION_SECRET}; a secret wins over a variable of the same name.

ingress.description: The preview's URLs by name, e.g. web: { service: web, port: 3000 }. When set, it replaces the dev.stagd.* labels in the compose file.

lifecycle.description: How long previews stay awake and live, in place of the org's setting.

previews.description: When pull requests get previews: when someone asks with /stagd deploy (on-demand, the default), always, or while they have a label.

registries.description: Logins for pulling private images, by the registry's host, e.g. ghcr.io.

services.description: What Stagd runs next to the app.

version.description: The file's format: 1, the only one so far.

wait.description: GitHub checks on the commit that must pass before it deploys, e.g. the workflow that pushes the images.

neon.description: A branch of a Neon database, forked for each preview.

Ingress.description: One of the preview's URLs: a service's port.

primary.description: The URL the pull request comment and the dashboard link to first.

Lifecycle.description: How long previews stay awake and live, in place of the org's setting.

expire_after.description: How long a preview lives without a new commit: 1h to 48h.

sleep_after.description: How long a preview nobody opens stays awake: 45m to 24h.

Neon.description: A Neon branch per preview, forked from a parent branch. Which parents may be forked is the org's Neon integration's to say: a pull request that could name any parent could fork production into its preview.

env.description: The variables the URLs are given as, by kind: url (pooled or not, as pooled says), pooled and unpooled. By default url: DATABASE_URL.

integration.description: Which of the org's Neon integrations, when it has several.

params.description: Added to the URLs, e.g. sslmode: verify-full.

parent.description: The branch to fork: its id or name.

pooled.description: Whether url is the pooled URL.

role.description: The role the URLs sign in as, neondb_owner by default.

export.description: Where a copy of what the app sends goes on to: the team's own backend.

ignore.description: Request paths whose traces aren't kept, a * matching the rest, e.g. [/healthz, /internal/*].

headers.description: Headers sent with it, e.g. Authorization: "Bearer ${DASH0_TOKEN}".

protocol.description: How it's sent: http/protobuf (the default) or grpc.

database.description: The database the app uses: postgres when left out.

seed.description: What the database starts with: an https URL of a pg_dump, plain SQL, custom or tar format, compressed with gzip or zstd or not. Restored once, when the preview is made; redeploys keep the data. It may use variables and secrets, e.g. https://example.com/seed.dump?${SEED_TOKEN}.

version.description: The major version: 16, 17, 18 (the default) or 19. A seed made with a newer pg_dump than this doesn't restore.

label.description: A GitHub label: adding it deploys the preview, removing it tears the preview down.

when.description: on-demand, when someone asks with /stagd deploy; or always.

anyOf.description: on-demand, when someone asks with /stagd deploy; or always.

Registry.description: A login for pulling images from one registry.

password.description: A secret of Stagd's, written as "${NAME}": a password in the repository is a leaked password.

Services.description: What Stagd runs next to the app.

mail.description: Captures the mail the app sends (Mailpit), for the dashboard and the preview's own inbox.

otel.description: An OpenTelemetry endpoint for the app's traces, with a viewer (Jaeger).

postgres.description: A Postgres database for the preview, started from a seed when there is one. The app gets its URL in DATABASE_URL.

checks.description: Check run or workflow names, e.g. [build-images]; one failing fails the preview at once.

timeout.description: How long to wait for them, from when the deploy starts: 30m by default, 1m to 2h.
